sections.title: Fats
sections.narration: 22.3 grams of fat. Saturated fat is 1.5 grams, supporting a cleaner fat profile. Polyunsaturated fat is 3.3 grams, not adding much polyunsaturated-fat support, so that's a real downside for seeds. For seeds, fat quality is a big reason to use them.

sections.title: Carbs
sections.narration: 44.2 grams of carbs. Starch is 11 grams, supporting useful staple-carb energy. Fibre is 10.5 grams, with only modest fullness and digestion support, so that's a small downside for seeds. For seeds, fibre matters much more than raw carb totals.

sections.narration: Positives first: richer texture can help satisfaction. That can make a small amount feel more useful in real meals. Easy to sprinkle into meals. sections.title: Cons
sections.narration: The drawbacks next: spice-like serving sizes limit real payoff. The numbers look huge, but people do not eat 100 grams of cumin seeds. Texture or prep can be a barrier. Not everyone uses seeds consistently. Paper scores can overstate realistic serving sizes. People often eat far less than 100 grams.
